en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 3 deals, the strategies behind them · 8 November 2026

🔹 Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) (port operations and logistics, the infrastructure arm of the Indian Adani conglomerate) acquires Evos B.V (bulk liquid storage, hydrocarbons, chemicals, biofuels via eight port terminals in the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Belgium) — €2.56bn.
Evos is Europe's second-largest independent bulk liquid storage operator, strategically located at the continent's major energy hubs.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Evos' terminals represent an infrastructure annuity: their value lies in their position within flows that industries cannot bypass, regardless of the type of liquid stored, making them compatible with the energy transition.

🔹 Viscofan Technology (Suzhou) (a subsidiary of Viscofan, a global specialist in casings for meat products, collagen, cellulose, plastic, and fiber) acquires Haiaos (production and distribution of collagen casings for meat processing, with a customer base and production capacity in China).
The agreement covers 58.94% of the capital, with a commitment to reach 85% by integrating other minority shareholders; the founders retain 15% with a call option on the third anniversary of closing.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Viscofan combines its technological expertise in collagen casings with Haiaos' local commercial and production base, preferring acquisition over organic growth, which is deemed too slow given Chinese regulatory barriers.

🔹 Royal Reesink (international distribution of agricultural machinery, green space equipment, construction machinery, handling equipment) acquires Price Turfcare (distribution of the Ventrac brand, professional tool carriers for turf maintenance and challenging terrains in the United Kingdom).
Price Turfcare will be absorbed by Reesink UK Ltd, which already distributes the Toro, BioCircle, Perrot, turfRad, and Agrimetal brands in these markets.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Royal Reesink is densifying its offering through network build-up: by integrating Ventrac distribution rights into an existing structure, it expands its brand portfolio without additional infrastructure costs.

🔗 These deals and those of your markets, every morning: https://proplace.co/actualites/?lang=en&secteurs=logistics-and-supply-chain,industrial-tech-and-manufacturing&type=ma

fr.text:
M&A : les 3 annonces récentes de l'édito du 8 novembre 2026.

🔹 Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) (𝑒𝑥𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑡𝑢𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒, 𝑏𝑟𝑎𝑠 𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒 𝑑𝑢 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑔𝑙𝑜𝑚𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑖𝑒𝑛 𝐴𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑖) rachète Evos B.V (𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑐𝑘𝑎𝑔𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑛 𝑣𝑟𝑎𝑐, ℎ𝑦𝑑𝑟𝑜𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑏𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑠, 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑡𝑠 𝑐ℎ𝑖𝑚𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠, 𝑏𝑖𝑜𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑏𝑢𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑠) — 2,56 Md€.
Evos est le deuxième opérateur indépendant européen de stockage de liquides en vrac, positionné sur les grands carrefours énergétiques du continent.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Les terminaux d'Evos constituent une rente d'infrastructure : leur valeur tient à leur position dans des flux que les industriels ne peuvent contourner, indépendamment du type de liquide stocké, ce qui les rend compatibles avec la transition énergétique.

🔹 Viscofan Technology (Suzhou) (𝑓𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑉𝑖𝑠𝑐𝑜𝑓𝑎𝑛, 𝑠𝑝𝑒́𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑖𝑎𝑙 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑛𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑠 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑡𝑠 𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑛𝑒́𝑠, 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑎𝑔𝑒̀𝑛𝑒) rachète Haiaos (𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑏𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑'𝑒𝑛𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑎𝑔𝑒̀𝑛𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙𝑎 𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑠𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑣𝑖𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑒).
L'accord porte sur 58,94 % du capital, avec engagement d'atteindre 85 % en intégrant d'autres minoritaires ; les fondateurs conservent 15 % avec option d'achat au troisième anniversaire du closing.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Viscofan combine son expertise technologique en enveloppes de collagène avec l'ancrage commercial et productif local de Haiaos, préférant l'acquisition à une croissance organique jugée trop lente face aux barrières réglementaires chinoises.

🔹 Royal Reesink (𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑏𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑚𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑖𝑠𝑚𝑒 𝑎𝑔𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑒, 𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑒́𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠 𝑒𝑠𝑝𝑎𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑣𝑒𝑟𝑡𝑠, 𝑒𝑛𝑔𝑖𝑛𝑠 𝑇𝑃) rachète Price Turfcare (𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑏𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑎 𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑉𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑐, 𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑡𝑒-𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑙𝑠 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑓𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑙𝑠).
Price Turfcare sera absorbée par Reesink UK Ltd, qui distribue déjà les marques Toro, BioCircle, Perrot, turfRad et Agrimetal sur ces marchés.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Royal Reesink densifie son offre par build-up de réseau : en intégrant les droits de distribution Ventrac dans une structure existante, il élargit son portefeuille de marques sans coût d'infrastructure supplémentaire.
